bios.Jesmond Gatt: Joined the Central Bank of Malta in 1984; graduated in Mathematics and Computing, University of Malta, 1995. Board member of the FIAU from 2016, Chairman from 2020-2023. CEO of Malta Government Investments before his MFSA appointment. bios.Kenneth Farrugia: Certified Public Accountant, fellow of the Malta Institute of Accountants; holds a Bachelor of Accountancy (Hons) and an MA in Business Ethics. Also serves as Chairman of the FIAU.

bios.Pierre Fenech: Chief Executive Officer of the Institute of Tourism Studies (ITS) — his sole government role since April 2025. He is himself an ITS graduate, holding a Diploma in Hospitality Management from the Institute, followed by a B.Com (Hons) in Tourism from the University of Malta and an Executive MBA. He began his career in food and beverage, event and general management roles at establishments including the Bugibba Holiday Complex, The Coastline Hotel and Island Caterers; in 2008 he was appointed Director of Operations and Quality Assurance at Island Caterers, a post he held until November 2012, when he became General Manager of MKIC Ltd, the company running Montekristo Estates on behalf of Island Hotels Group. In March 2015 he was appointed CEO of the Mediterranean Conference Centre (MCC), and later also took on the CEO role at ITS, holding both positions concurrently for years — an arrangement local media dubbed him the tourism sector's "Super CEO" for. In March 2025, Tourism Minister Ian Borg did not renew his MCC contract; Nigel Vella was appointed to succeed him at the MCC from April 2025, and Fenech has continued solely as CEO of ITS since. He has faced two notable controversies: in 2019 he gave Labour MP Rosianne Cutajar a paid consultancy contract later described as a "phantom" job, since she was found to have done little to no work for the payment — a Standards Commissioner probe questioned the ethics of the arrangement but did not find Fenech personally at fault, since the tourism ministry's then permanent secretary, Anthony Gatt, had approved the related expenses (Gatt was subsequently removed from the post); and in 2021 he issued a direct order using ITS funds to architect Gilbert Bartolo, who was the brother of then-Tourism Minister Clayton Bartolo, saying he was not aware of the family relationship at the time.

bios.Dr Simon Micallef Stafrace: President of the Medical Council Malta, appointed by the Prime Minister for the term 22 August 2023 to 21 August 2026. Holds an LL.D. and a Master of Laws (LL.M.). Chairs the Council's Sub-Committee for the Analyses of Complaints (SCAC). The Medical Council Malta regulates medical practitioners and dental surgeons under the Health Care Professions Act (Chapter 464 of the Laws of Malta), maintaining the statutory Medical Register.
bios.Dr Joseph Chetcuti: President of the Pharmacy Council, appointed by the Prime Minister for the term running until 22 August 2026. bios.Dr Simon Cachia: President of the Council for Nurses and Midwives (CNM), appointed by the Minister for Health and Active Ageing for a three-year term from 13 January 2026 per the Government Gazette, having also served the preceding one-year term from January 2025. bios.Dr Oliver de Gaetano: President of the Council for the Professions Complementary to Medicine (CPCM) since July 2022, the statutory body regulating 20 health care professions in Malta including physiotherapy, dietetics, occupational therapy, radiography and podiatry among others. bios.Mr Oliver Scicluna: Chief Executive Officer of Aġenzija Sapport, Malta's national agency providing services and support to persons with disabilities and their families. bios.Mr Frederick Schembri: President of the Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology (MCAST), per the College's official profile.
bios.Mr Stephen Vella: Principal and Chief Executive Officer of the Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology (MCAST). Educated at Savio College, Stella Maris College, the University of Malta and Falkirk College of Arts in Scotland, with an MBA from Henley School of Management. Began his career teaching Graphic Design and Photography at Salvatore Dimech School for Craftsmen in 1993, rising to Deputy Director in 2003, and has spent over twenty years across MCAST's institutes and corporate structure. Represented MCAST at Prof. Frank Bezzina's installation as University of Malta Rector in June 2026, and publicly defended MCAST's funding model in March 2026 following comments by the outgoing UM Rector about the University's financial deficit.

Also recorded is Prof. Bezzina's concurrent role as an Accountancy Board member and Central Bank of Malta director, per prior research in this project - a genuine cross-appointment.

bios.Prof. Frank Bezzina: Rector of the University of Malta, unanimously elected by the University Council on 26 March 2026 as the sole nominee, beginning his five-year term on 1 July 2026 and succeeding Prof. Alfred J. Vella. Outlined a vision of the University as a strategic national institution during his Council presentation titled 'Knowledge for the common good.' Also serves as a Board Member of the Accountancy Board and a Director on the Board of the Central Bank of Malta, per prior research in this project.

Cuschieri was controversially given a new MCAST consultancy role, recommended by the Education Minister. bios.Dr Edward Woods: Chairman of the Malta Further and Higher Education Authority (MFHEA). A lawyer (LL.D.) specialising in Civil and Commercial Law, with a focus on Marine Disputes, Business Partnerships and Property Law. Extensive public board history: former Chairman of the Malta Maritime Authority, former Chairman of the Malta Communications Authority, Member of the Board of Governors of the Malta Arbitration Centre, and involvement in the Valletta Cruise Liner Terminal Project.
bios.Mr James Perry Maia: Chief Executive Officer of the Malta Further and Higher Education Authority (MFHEA), appointed October 2025, succeeding Dr Rose Anne Cuschieri. Over two decades of experience in education leadership, quality assurance and institutional governance. Previously Deputy Director at MCAST's Institute of Business Management and Commerce; also held senior roles as CEO of the Federation of English Language Teaching Organisations Malta (FELTOM), Executive Director of the Archbishop's Seminary, Deputy/Acting Director at the Institute of Tourism Studies, and Accreditation Officer at the former National Commission for Further and Higher Education. Represented Malta internationally on ECVET and EQAVET frameworks.
bios.Mr Anthony Borg: Board Member of the Malta Further and Higher Education Authority (MFHEA). Extensive Civil Service career holding executive positions across the Ministries of Finance, Works, Social Services, Parliament and the Office of the Prime Minister; appointed Director on the Boards of ARMS, ERL, MECS and MITA.
bios.Mr Anatole: Board Member of the Malta Further and Higher Education Authority (MFHEA), as listed on the Authority's own Board Members page (full surname not captured in the available source). Graduated with a Doctorate in Law from the University of Malta in 2003 and was admitted to the Maltese Bar in 2004. Member of the Chamber of Advocates and the Institute of Financial Services Practitioners; has delivered lectures and seminars on specialist legal subjects.

bios.Joseph Azzopardi: Member of the Malta Financial Services Tribunal (MFST), appointed 2015. Fellow of the Chartered Association of Certified Accountants (FCCA), holds a practising warrant in auditing, and is a graduate MBA from Warwick Business School. Worked at a Big Five audit firm in Malta and overseas, lectured at the University of Malta's Department of Management, and served as an advisory partner in a mid-tier audit firm. bios.Dr Stephanie Fabri: Council Member of the Malta Fiscal Advisory Council (MFAC), joined 10 January 2023. Resident academic at the University of Malta specialising in strategic management and public policy; also a non-executive director at a private company.
bios.Dr Stephanie Vella: Council Member of the Malta Fiscal Advisory Council (MFAC), joined 10 January 2023. Notably, Dr Reno Borg previously served as Malta's first Financial Services Arbiter - a connection relevant to the 'Arbiter for Financial Services' entity under MFF, which remains unresolved; it is possible but not confirmed that Borg's successor there is now known.

bios.Dr Reno Borg: Information and Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC) of Malta, sworn in 24 April 2026 for a five-year term, succeeding Ian Deguara. A lawyer by background, formerly worked at the Office of the Attorney General and served as Malta's first Financial Services Arbiter, as well as chairman of several state institutions. Minister for Justice and Reform of the Construction Sector Jonathan Attard praised his 'strong legal background and extensive experience' at the swearing-in. Responsible for enforcing the Data Protection Act, GDPR, the Freedom of Information Act, and the Re-Use of Public Sector Information Act.

bios.Silvio Scerri: Chief Executive Officer of Xjenza Malta, the government agency acting as Malta's national R&D and Space funding agency, and the policy development and implementation body for Research, Innovation and Space, confirmed via the agency's own Management Team page.

Malta Arbitration Centre.note: Board of Governors legally consists of 3-5 members; only 3 (Chairman, Deputy Chairperson, one Member) were confirmed via individual bio pages on the Centre's own site as of this check - the full complement may include 1-2 further members not individually profiled.

bios.Dr Paul Cachia: Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Malta Arbitration Centre, appointed 2019 after previously serving as a Board member. An advocate specialising in cross-border litigation, civil, commercial, constitutional and human rights litigation in the Courts of Malta. Holds a first-class B.A. in Legal & Humanistic Studies, Diploma of Notary Public, LL.D. (2003), and a Magister Juris and M.Phil from the University of Oxford as a Chevening Scholar. Worked as a lawyer with the European Commission in Brussels (2008-2010); chaired the Civil Justice Working Parties during Malta's EU Council Presidency and continues to represent Malta on the Council's Civil Law Working Party. Former visiting lecturer at the University of Malta on the Law of Tort and Private International Law.
bios.Dr Anna Mallia: Deputy Chairperson of the Board of Governors of the Malta Arbitration Centre, appointed 2019 after previously serving as a Board member. An advocate specialising in civil law, family law, public procurement, industrial law, and data protection and freedom of information, practising in the Courts of Malta. Graduated Notary Public (1984) and Doctor of Laws (1986) from the University of Malta; was part of the Maltese delegation in the Malta-Libya case at the International Court of Justice in The Hague. A Chevening Scholar, Commonwealth Scholar and Hubert Humphrey Alumnus.
bios.Dr Chris Cilia: Member of the Board of Governors of the Malta Arbitration Centre since 2019. Has served for a number of years as Deputy Chairman of the Malta Gaming Authority and currently serves as Deputy Chairman of Indis Malta Ltd, as well as director on several public liability private companies.
bios.Dr Fiona Galea Farrugia: Registrar of the Malta Arbitration Centre, who also serves as Secretary to the Board of Governors and holds legal representation of the Centre, including the power to administer oaths of office for arbitrators.

bios.Eunice Grech Fiorini: Director (Chief Executive) of the Asset Recovery Bureau, appointed 24 March 2025, succeeding Anthony Sevasta. bios.Vanessa Grech: Chief Executive Officer of the Courts Services Agency, appointed 24 March 2025, succeeding Eunice Grech Fiorini. A lawyer with 27 years of public service experience across almost every section of the Courts of Justice, first joining as a clerk in August 1998. In the four years prior to her appointment she served as Deputy Chief Executive, Director of Legal Services, legal advisor to the Court, and Registrar of Civil Courts and Tribunals. Also contributed to formulating Malta's position on EU-related issues concerning the Agency.

Office of the Attorney General.note: In post since September 2020; Malta's first female Attorney General, appointed via independent selection committee following constitutional reforms separating the AG's prosecutorial role from the State Advocate's advisory role. Confirmed still current via a Wikidata reference retrieved 20 April 2026.

bios.Victoria Buttigieg: Attorney General of Malta since September 2020, and the first woman to hold the office. Graduated Doctor of Laws from the University of Malta in 2001 and later obtained a Master of Arts in Financial Services. Joined the Office of the Attorney General in 2007, becoming Deputy Attorney General in 2012, heading the departments of Civil Law, Administrative Law and Constitutional Law. Appointed Malta's first State Advocate in December 2019, before being appointed Attorney General the following year, succeeding Peter Grech. Was one of three candidates considered for the AG post by an independent selection committee following the constitutional reform splitting prosecutorial and advisory legal functions.

Office of the State Advocate.note: Confirmed current as of January 2024 (attendance at a magistrates' swearing-in) and March 2024 (court testimony in the Vitals hospitals civil case). Succeeded Victoria Buttigieg, Malta's first State Advocate, when she became Attorney General in 2020.

bios.Chris Soler: State Advocate of Malta, the chief legal advisor to the Government on constitutional, civil and administrative law matters, succeeding Victoria Buttigieg when she was appointed Attorney General in 2020. Also serves as Malta's Agent before the International Court of Justice. Publicly testified in March 2024 in the Nationalist Party's civil case seeking to recover damages related to the Vitals/Steward hospitals concession, stating that his office could only act on matters where the law gave it a specific right to, or when instructed by government.
